slot.brief: Order a primary aliphatic amine, a secondary amine, an aryl amine and ammonia by basic strength in aqueous solution; include steric and solvation effects.

stem: In aqueous solution, which is the decreasing order of basic strength, taking solvation and resonance into account?

verdicts.working: In water, methyl groups increase basicity by their electron-donating effect; dimethylamine is slightly more basic than methylamine. Aniline is weakest because resonance delocalizes the nitrogen lone pair. Thus the order is (CH₃)₂NH > CH₃NH₂ > NH₃ > C₆H₅NH₂.

working:
In water: secondary alkyl amine $>$ primary alkyl amine $>$ $\text{NH}_3$.
Alkyl groups increase electron density at N; aqueous solvation favors the secondary amine over the primary amine.
In aniline, the lone pair is delocalized into the ring, so it is less basic than $\text{NH}_3$.

Independent check: In water, methyl groups increase basicity by their electron-donating effect; dimethylamine is slightly more basic than methylamine. Aniline is weakest because resonance delocalizes the nitrogen lone pair. Thus the order is (CH₃)₂NH > CH₃NH₂ > NH₃ > C₆H₅NH₂.
solution:
Alkyl groups donate electron density to nitrogen; in water, solvation gives $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{NH}>\text{CH}_3\text{NH}_2>\text{NH}_3$. In aniline, resonance delocalizes the lone pair, making it less available for protonation.
$$ (\text{CH}_3)_2\text{NH}>\text{CH}_3\text{NH}_2>\text{NH}_3>\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{NH}_2 $$
